purpose: Clemastine is used to relieve allergy symptoms like runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and hives. It can also help with itchy skin caused by allergic reactions. It is available over the counter and by prescription.
how_it_works: When you have an allergic reaction, your body releases a chemical called histamine, which causes those uncomfortable symptoms. Clemastine works by blocking the receptors that histamine attaches to, so the histamine cannot cause as much trouble. Think of it like putting a lock on the door so histamine cannot get in and cause symptoms.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is drowsiness or feeling sleepy, which can be strong with this medication. You may also experience dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, constipation, or difficulty urinating. Some people feel a little foggy or have trouble concentrating.
warnings: Because clemastine causes significant drowsiness, do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how it affects you. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication as it makes the drowsiness much worse. Talk to your doctor before using it if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, breathing problems, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It is generally not recommended for young children without doctor guidance.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 1.34 mg (one tablet) taken twice a day, or 2.68 mg taken up to three times a day for more severe symptoms. Always follow the directions on the package or from your doctor. Try to take it at the same times each day, and it can be taken with or without food.
